newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies up limit on CME data, stops.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies up limit on CME data, stops.

text.p: August and February CME pork belly futures ran up the 3.000-cent-per-lb daily limit as demand sparked by a bullish CME Out-of-Town report ignited further buy stops, traders said.
August posted a limit gain of 3.000 cents at 91.750 cents per lb and February at 77.900 cents. Other months were up as much as 2.950 cents before meeting profit taking resistance, traders noted.
The out-of-town report showed another large out-movement last week compared with an in-movement last year, they said.
CME reported a net out-movement of 952,000 lbs last week at warehouses outside Chicago which compared with an in-movement of 333,000 lbs last year.
Out-of-town stocks are now only slightly above last year and may decline below year ago as storings are seen light or declining most of May, traders said.
